summary: Prefix cache shows ~0% reuse for streaming chat (same conversation) on Hosted API route; misses appear as hash_mismatch
description:
Issue summary
Aurora reports that prefix cache/KV cache reuse is effectively zero for their streaming chat workload, even when sending the same multi-turn conversation repeatedly. They expected high reuse because their support-agent flow replays a stable system + tool instructions prefix for every end-user message.

Impact
- Prefill latency higher than expected (customer reported ~1.7–2.2s p95 prefill vs ~0.9–1.2s historically)
- Cost increased due to repeated prefill (customer estimated ~30–45% token cost increase for their route)
- Customer sees "MISS" on every streamed response header and no improvement across repeated runs

Customer environment
- Deployment: Hosted API (Dedicated capacity)
- Region: us-east
- Model: llama-3-70b-instruct
- Endpoint: /v1/chat.completions (stream=true)
- Route: aurora-prod/support-agent-stream (as referenced by customer)

What the customer sees
- Response headers consistently show:
  - x-redwood-prefix-cache: MISS
  - x-redwood-kv-cache: MISS
- They tried sending the same conversation 10 times; saw 0 hits.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided)
1) Send a streaming chat request with stable system prompt + tools.
2) Repeat the exact same request (same messages array content) within ~30 seconds.
3) Expect: prefix reuse / shorter prefill / cache HIT headers.
4) Actual: always MISS.

Customer sample request (redacted)
- stream: true
- messages (high level):
  - system: "You are Aurora Support Agent..." + "Current time: <ISO timestamp>" + "session_id=<uuid>"
  - developer: tool instructions + JSON schema for tools
  - user: "Where is my order?"
- tools: array generated per-request from their orchestrator (customer noted it may be re-ordered across runs)

Customer-provided request IDs / trace IDs (redacted)
- req_id: rw_req_01J3A2KQ9D8P7M9XK9J5, trace_id: 7c3f1c7b1c2c2c1a
- req_id: rw_req_01J3A2N4TQ1G4YV9QH2B, trace_id: 7c3f1c7b1c2c2c4e
- req_id: rw_req_01J3A2QWQ62C1W8Z9F1H, trace_id: 7c3f1c7b1c2c2c93

Initial hypothesis
Likely cache-key instability in streaming chat due to:
- Volatile tokens embedded in the prefix (timestamps, UUID/session IDs)
- Non-canonical ordering of tool definitions (JSON key ordering / array order)
- Route-level caching policy disabled for streaming routes (some customers disable caching to avoid cross-request contamination; should be isolated by tenant/route, but route policy may be set to off)

Redwood investigation notes (internal)
- Pulled sampled cache telemetry for Aurora route in us-east: prefix reuse near zero and misses predominantly align with "hash_mismatch" (not capacity/eviction).
- Cross-checked gateway route config: route had prefix caching disabled (legacy setting from initial onboarding) and would not attempt prefix cache on stream=true.
- Even after temporarily enabling prefix caching on the route, we still saw low reuse in traces when customer’s system message included per-request timestamps and when tools were reordered across calls.

Resolution / guidance provided
1) Prompt canonicalization guidance (customer action)
- Remove volatile fields from the cacheable prefix:
  - Do NOT include timestamps, UUIDs, request IDs, or per-session IDs in system/developer messages if you expect prefix reuse.
  - If you must include them, move them to a non-cached suffix (e.g., last user message) or to request metadata that does not affect the prompt.
- Stabilize tool definition ordering:
  - Ensure tools[] array is deterministically ordered (e.g., sort by tool name).
  - Ensure JSON schemas are stable (no random key ordering; avoid injecting dynamic descriptions).
- Normalize whitespace:
  - Avoid templating that changes spacing/newlines across requests.

2) Route configuration fix (Redwood action)
- Enabled prefix caching for route aurora-prod/support-agent-stream (was disabled).
- Verified route isolates cache by tenant + route + model version to prevent cross-tenant leakage.

3) Verification after changes
- Customer reran repeated conversations (same prefix, stable tools ordering) and reported:
  - x-redwood-prefix-cache transitioned from MISS-only to mixed HIT/MISS
  - Observed faster time-to-first-token on repeat prompts
- Internal sampling showed prefix cache hit-rate rising to ~35–50% on their route during steady-state traffic, with corresponding reduction in wasted prefill.

Workaround snippet (shared with customer)
- Make the "prefix" stable:
  - system: "You are Aurora Support Agent..."  (no timestamp/session_id)
  - developer: stable tool instructions
  - tools: deterministically sorted
- Keep volatile data in the user message only, when possible.

Notes / caveats shared with customer
- Streaming retry behavior: if the client retries mid-stream with slightly different request bodies, it will not hit the same cache key.
- Model version: cache keys are scoped to model version; if you auto-upgrade models, hit-rate may reset until new prefixes are warmed.

Next steps
- Support to follow up in 1 week to confirm sustained hit-rate and ensure no unexpected cache behavior.
- Internal: capture this as a docs snippet for "Streaming chat + caching" best practices and add a Console hint when cache misses are dominated by hash_mismatch.
comments: 2025-03-22 (Owen Phillips, Support): Customer reports prefix cache not working for streaming chat. They see x-redwood-prefix-cache: MISS on every response. Asked for route name, request IDs, and whether their system prompt includes any dynamic values (timestamps/session IDs).

2025-03-22 (Customer - Aurora Support): Shared 3 request IDs and confirmed they include "Current time: <timestamp>" and a per-session UUID in system prompt for debugging. Also noted tools list is generated per request and may be in different order. They expected caching to ignore these differences.

2025-03-23 (Miguel Santos, CS): Reproduced behavior in principle: any change in the prompt prefix will change the cache key. For now cache is based on canonicalized request content; volatile tokens will prevent hits. Flagged to Runtime/Telemetry that misses appear consistent with hash mismatch rather than eviction.

2025-03-24 (Ethan Park, Platform): Checked route config: aurora-prod/support-agent-stream had prefix caching disabled (legacy onboarding default). Proposed enabling prefix cache on the route and monitoring for any anomaly.

2025-03-24 (Miguel Santos, CS): Updated customer with two likely causes: (1) route-level caching disabled; (2) cache-key instability due to timestamp/uuid + tools order. Provided prompt canonicalization checklist and asked them to test with static prefix and sorted tools.

2025-03-25 (Amara Diallo, Platform): Enabled prefix caching for route aurora-prod/support-agent-stream in prod us-east. Confirmed isolation scope is tenant+route+model_version and no cross-tenant sharing.

2025-03-26 (Customer - Aurora Support): Removed timestamp + uuid from system prompt; moved session_id to app logs only. Sorted tools array by name. Retested 10x: now sees intermittent x-redwood-prefix-cache: HIT and faster TTFT on repeats. Still sees MISS when tool schema changes.

2025-03-27 (Miguel Santos, CS): Confirmed expected behavior: any tool schema change alters the prompt and therefore the cache key. Recommended pinning tool schema per route version and rolling it like a deploy. Offered to help set up a "support-agent-v4" route to keep schemas stable.

2025-03-29 (Owen Phillips, Support): Customer confirmed hit-rate improvement is sufficient; cost trending down. Marking Resolved. Follow-up task: add a public docs/Console note on streaming chat prompt canonicalization and tool ordering for prefix cache.
resolution: Resolved by (1) enabling prefix caching on the customer’s streaming chat route (it was disabled), and (2) advising customer to canonicalize the cacheable prefix by removing volatile tokens (timestamps/session UUIDs) and making tool definitions deterministically ordered. After changes, customer observed cache HIT headers and improved TTFT/cost on repeat prompts.
internal_notes: Telemetry indicates misses were dominated by hash_mismatch, not eviction/capacity. This ticket is a good example for recommendations MVP: detect high hash_mismatch rate + high wasted prefill on a route and suggest prompt canonicalization + tool ordering + verify route cache policy enabled.
